html:
The Snohomish are a Coast Salish people of the lower Snohomish River and the shores of Puget Sound around today's Everett, Washington. They speak Lushootseed, like their neighbours the Stillaguamish, Skagit and Snoqualmie.

They lived in cedar plank houses at the river mouth and on Whidbey Island, fishing for salmon and gathering shellfish. In 1855 their leaders signed the Treaty of Point Elliott at Mukilteo, giving up most of their land. Many moved to the Tulalip reservation, created on Snohomish land. The Snohomish Tribe, made up of families who did not move, is still seeking federal recognition.
